item.title: [492] You do not need your gaming hardware.
item.description:
Sam Altman calls out greedy and selfish personal computer owners. You do not need 32GB RAM. It needs to be in a data center where it can be utilized properly. People hoarding RAM for their insignificant private needs is nothing but public greed. Which one is more important? Progress and an American company winning the AI race, or your bing bing wahoo video games on PC?

>Over the past year, memory prices have skyrocketed to support the demands of AI. Not only has consumer hardware suffered as a result, but memory manufacturer Micron even announced its departure from consumer memory production as a result. The company claimed that the needs of AI datacentres are “essential” compared to consumer use.
>In an interview with Cheeky Pint, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman argued that one of the issues keeping the memory supply chain strained is the want for local compute by everyday people. While large-scale LLMs ran at datacentres by massive companies are the most known forms of AI, Altman believes locally-run models—which are arguably far more sustainable—are an issue.
>The tech billionaire argued that “from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer. And be used 5% of the time.” While OpenAI is allowed to buy up 40% of the global DRAM output, Altman believes the 32GB of RAM sitting in your computer is tantamount to public greed.

https://frvr.com/blog/news/openai-ceo-sam-altman-says-its-terrible-to-have-everybody-have-a-bunch-of-the-worlds-limited-supply-of-dram-instead-of-shoving-it-all-in-datacentres/

item.title: [ 52] Countdown to trump's next coup, Republican governor will refuse to certify Democratic victory
item.description:
https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6182999-alaska-election-verification-stopped-peltola-probe/
Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy (R) suggested Thursday his state’s midterm election certification process may be “stopped or changed” because of its investigation into ballot-stacking allegations against Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola.

NewsNation’s Blake Burman asked Dunleavy about the state’s probe into Peltola, which the governor announced earlier that day, and whether it could impact how election officials plan to certify midterm winners.

“We are going to investigate it. We’re going to follow the law,” Dunleavy told Burman. “We are ready to do whatever we need to do to ensure that our elections are deemed credible.”

“If we find out there’s wrongdoing, and if that means that the certification then is stopped or changed, then that’s what happens,” the governor added later in the conversation.

Burman then pressed Dunleavy on whether he believes there’s a legitimate possibility Alaska may need to stop or change its election certification, to which the GOP governor responded, “Depending upon the outcomes of this investigation, yes.”

The New York Times reported Wednesday Peltola’s campaign recruited a man named Dan J. Sullivan to run against incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) in an effort to confuse voters. Peltola is challenging the GOP lawmaker in the Alaska Senate race.

The former congresswoman’s campaign has denied it played a role in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan.

Two conservative political commenters have now been charged for their polling place impersonation, in which they highlighted Minnesota’s vouching laws during the state’s primary election.

The complaints charge James O’Keefe and Cam Higby, members of the Florida-based O’Keefe Media Group, with identity theft and unlawful voting.

Back in August, the two shared videos online in which at least one member of the “Justice League” is dressed in a burqa, and another man in the video can be heard using an accent to try to vouch for others.
What Happened?

In the video posted online, someone in the O’Keefe and Higby group gave the first name “William” to a poll worker at Pratt Elementary School. When asked for a last name, they responded, “Pomeranz,” and then proceeded to ask about the state’s vouching law.

William Pomeranz is an actual registered voter in Minneapolis, although O’Keefe’s group said in a statement that, “The Justice League did not impersonate anyone. At no point did we claim to be William Pomerantz or any other voter. We stated a name and asked election workers questions about Minnesota’s vouching process.”

A man in the video can be heard using an accent to try to vouch for others, but O’Keefe’s group apparently left the polling place after being told he needed to sign an oath to vouch for someone.

Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon says 0.6% of Minnesota voters were vouched for in 2024 — and Simon says he does not recall a case of vouching fraud during his tenure. However, it’s up to local prosecutors to file charges for any election malfeasance, not the Secretary of State’s Office, which did confirm in August that law enforcement was “reviewing” the O’Keefe group video.

https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2026/10/28/hasan-piker-sues-cnn-commentator-scott-jennings-for-725-million-over-manipulated-video/

Left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a $72.5 million defamation lawsuit against conservative pundit and CNN contributor Scott Jennings on Tuesday, alleging that Jennings falsely accused him of calling for the lynching of Black Americans by airing an edited video from a 2024 livestream on his show.

Key Facts
>In a filing made before the D.C. federal court, Piker accused Jennings of defamation, defamation by implication, and portraying him in a false light, and is seeking $27.5 million in compensatory damages and $45 million in punitive damages.

>The complaint centers on the August 11 episode of the conservative pundit’s radio program and podcast, The Scott Jennings Show, where Piker alleges Jennings falsely told listeners that the streamer had a “plan of returning our country to lynchings,” while airing a misleading video of his remarks.

>The 42-second video that aired on Jennings’ show was shared by the National Republican Senatorial Committee five days earlier on X, and appeared to show Piker describing himself as a “racist” and expressing support for a return to an era of lynchings.

>The filing alleges that the video combined footage from three separate Twitch livestreams, rearranged the sequence of Piker’s remarks, and edited out the YouTube debate between two Black political commentators that the streamer was reacting to.

>Piker’s lawyers allege the clip omitted his opening words, “He said,” from remarks in which he was sarcastically mocking a Black conservative commentator featured in the YouTube debate who had blamed “woke DAs” for policies harming Black Americans, making it appear as though Piker was expressing his own views.

item.title: [ 82] /out/ings with a Pipe Autumn Edition
item.description:
Last thread >>2868475

This is a thread for enjoying a pipe while doing outdoor activities. If you ask why this belongs on /out/, you've never spent
an evening by the campfire with a pipe silently enjoying the nature around you, and you're missing out.

>how to get started
Purchase a corn cob pipe (or a cheap briar pipe) and a pouch of Half and Half or Captain Black tobacco from a smoke shop
or online. You will need a lighter or match, and something to tamp it with--a large nail works well if you don't have a pipe tool.
Fill the pipe with tobacco, pack it down halfway, top it off, pack it down to 3/4, top it off again, pack gently and enjoy. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the tobacco tastes best when it is burning cool. Tamp and re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you.
>smoking a pipe will give you cancer
Originally the Surgeon General found that pipe and cigar smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when
most adults smoked, so they had a good sample size), had insignificant death rate increases. Nowadays, tobacco is being
legislated against while hard drugs are being legalized. Put two and two together. Tobacco is just another good thing under attack by the government.

>muh weed
Not the time or place. Start your own thread.

All tobacco users welcome.

item.title: [143] Moving to England
item.description:
How bad of an idea would it be for an American to attempt to move to England? I'm finishing graduate school soon, and I don't want to look for a job in the US. I've visited England 6 times, but what is it like to actually live here?

My main motivation is the public transport. I absolutely fucking hate driving. It terrifies me. I don't understand why something so dangerous and so expensive is widely accepted as being a necessity for everyday life. It is ruining my life, because my country has no good public transport.

Many other European countries have good public transport, but I only speak English. Would I regret moving here? I love English people, and have several close friends who live there. I would only want to live somewhere that I can actually meet people, so no rural hamlets.
